subject: Payment terms and staging proposal for Spotlight Health pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.in>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@spotlighthealth.com>, procurement@spotlighthealth.com
Cc: karl@spotlighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Payment terms and staging proposal for Spotlight Health pilot

Hi Lisa / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get the pilot scoped. A couple of items we wanted to align on before we finalize the SOW: payment schedule, net terms, and a short-term credit guardrail so both teams have clarity during ramp. High-level proposal below: 

- Pilot fee: $95,000 total for 90 days (see attached SOW).
- Initial deposit: $25,000 due at signature (applied to first invoice).
- Remaining invoicing: two invoices during the pilot: Day 30 (net 45) and Day 60 (net 45) after invoice date.
- Standard net term: Net45 for invoices after the deposit.
- Conditional credit cap: cumulative spend max $150k without a separate credit application. If consumption exceeds this, we require a completed credit application and a short approval window (5 business days).
- VAT/tax: we will invoice Spotlight Health Ltd. We need your VAT registration or confirmation of reverse-charge eligibility (see tax checklist).

Attachments: Spotlight_SOW_v2.pdf, Invoice_Schedule_Spotlight.csv.

Ask: Can you confirm if the deposit + Net45 cadence works for Spotlight Health, and whether procurement needs a PO ahead of signature? If Net45 is problematic, we can discuss Net60 with an increased deposit.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.in | +1 415-555-0123

From: Lisa Chen <lisa@spotlighthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.in>
Cc: procurement@spotlighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Payment terms and staging proposal for Spotlight Health pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) VAT/tax: Spotlight Health is a UK-registered entity; we generally apply reverse charge but procurement will want a written confirmation and a copy of the Redwoods VAT registration number.
2) Net45 is preferable to Net30, but given our internal payment calendar we usually push Net60. We could accept Net45 for the pilot if there is an increased deposit to cover cashflow.
3) Credit cap: procurement will need the company's standard credit application and a list of references if we were to increase the cap beyond $150k. Will the credit application only require financials/ref-checks or also proof of insurance?

I've pasted your key points below for context. Procurement — can you confirm the PO process (lead time + required docs)?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@spotlighthealth.com>, procurement@spotlighthealth.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.in>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment terms and staging proposal for Spotlight Health pilot

Hi Lisa — Karthik here from Finance, looping in to clarify the VAT and credit path so procurement has everything in one place. Thanks Jordan for the draft. Short answers up front: we can support reverse-charge invoicing to a UK entity, and the credit application is fairly lightweight for increases up to $500k. Details below and a couple of asks.

VAT / Tax handling:
- If Spotlight Health provides a valid UK VAT registration number and confirms reverse charge eligibility, we'll issue invoices without UK VAT and include the reverse charge note. Please attach your VAT certificate or a VAT number verification link.
- If the bill-to is a US entity or there is a cross-entity scenario, we will route tax differently — call this out in the SOW.

Credit cap and timing:
- The standard credit application we use is attached (redwood-credit-application.pdf). For caps up to $150k we typically accept a signed application + trade reference (no audited financials). For increases beyond $150k we will require more detailed references and a short underwriting call (usually 3–5 business days).
- Insurance: we request general liability coverage but don't require certificate upload for the initial cap. We will request COI for caps > $250k.

Alternative cadence option (if Net60 is mandatory):
- Deposit increases to $40,000 at signature, then two subsequent invoices Net60. This reduces Redwood's exposure but keeps operations simple for Spotlight.

Requested docs to proceed:
- VAT registration / reverse-charge confirmation (PDF or verification link)
- Completed redwood-credit-application.pdf (attached) if you anticipate exceeding the $150k cap
- PO number if procurement requires it to release deposit invoice

I've attached a short tax-evidence-checklist.xlsx that outlines exactly what we need to apply reverse-charge cleanly.

If you confirm which cadence works (Net45 with $25k deposit vs Net60 with $40k deposit), Jordan will update the SOW and DocuSign link.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.in

(attachments: redwood-credit-application.pdf, tax-evidence-checklist.xlsx)
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@spotlighthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.in>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.in>
Cc: procurement@spotlighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 16:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Payment terms and staging proposal for Spotlight Health pilot

Thanks Karthik — that helps a lot. Procurement confirms they can do Net45 for the pilot if the deposit is increased to $40k and we provide the VAT verification.

Decision:
- Spotlight Health will sign under the UK entity and provide VAT registration by tomorrow.
- We will accept Net45 on the two subsequent invoices during the 90-day pilot with a $40,000 deposit at signature.
- We will not require a full credit check now; procurement will process the credit application only if we ramp past $150k.

Next steps for Jordan: please push an updated SOW reflecting the $40k deposit and the Net45 cadence and send a DocuSign link for signature. Procurement will issue a PO once the deposit invoice is received.
